messages:
maria (eng-runtime): noticed a big p95/p99 regression on prod after last night
update. affected customers on rwd-4x when sequence lengths >1500. p95 went from ~120ms to ~700ms, p99 spiking to 2s+. started ~2026-03-14T05:12Z (see deploy-bot below).

taylor (support): customer reported slow responses and timeouts for chat sessions (request ids: abc123, def456). they're pretty upset; said it started after the platform update.

ajay (eng-sre): timeline? which deploy? single region? any correlation with infra changes (kernel, driver, entropy)?

maria (eng-runtime): deploy-bot shows a runtime build rolled at 05:12 UTC to all-hosted. commit 6f3a2b8 changed attention kernel selection and compile flags.
deploy-bot: release 2026-03-14T05:12:00 - runtime-service v3.8.1 deployed to hosted-prod (canary -> global). changelog: "enable SDPA fused kernels, prefer sdpa when available".

lin (eng-ml): ugly but expected. the SDPA/FlashAttention toggle in 6f3a2b8 switched the kernel selection heuristic to prefer SDPA for certain matmul shapes. for long sequences SDPA path increases memory traffic and sometimes regresses latency due to different block tiling. commit: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/6f3a2b8

ryan (build): i can revert the compile flag quickly or push a hotfix build with SDPA disabled (build tag -DFLASHATTN=OFF). that takes ~20-30min to build + ~15min to canary.

maria (eng-runtime): need faster mitigation - customers are in prod. options: 1) runtime env override to force legacy kernels, 2) per-customer routing to older model variant, 3) immediate rollback of deploy. prefer 1+2 to avoid full rollback.

ajay (eng-sre): let's do both: set env override globally for hosted-prod to disable sdpa/fused-attn, and route affected customer(s) to rwd-4x@v1.1 (previous). i can put a temporary routing rule.

lin (eng-ml): env var we have: REDWOOD_PREFER_SDPA=true/false. also runtime supports REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=legacy|sdpa|auto. set REDWOOD_PREFER_SDPA=false and REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=legacy in canary and then promote. example:

```
# internal control plane call
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/configs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"env": {"REDWOOD_PREFER_SDPA": "false", "REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE": "legacy"}, "scope": "hosted-prod"}'
```

maria (eng-runtime): repro steps I've been running locally: seq_len=2048, batch=1, model=rwd-4x, prompt minimal. run:

```
# small repro
python benchmarks/latency.py --model rwd-4x --seq 2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 --endpoint https://api.redwood.ai/generate --api-key $KEY
```

logs (before->after deploy):
```
# before (v3.7.x)
p50: 55ms, p95: 120ms, p99: 240ms
# after (v3.8.1)
p50: 60ms, p95: 700ms, p99: 2100ms
```

ryan (build): pushing a hotfix build that compiles with -DFLASHATTN=OFF now. i'll kick it and ping when canary is up.

ajay (eng-sre): i've applied a routing rule to send customer X (org: bigchat) to rwd-4x@v1.1 immediately, and created a temporary quota increase so requests don't queue. watch metrics.

sam (customer-success): i'll notify the customer that we have a mitigation (routing + kernel override) and an ETA for a permanent fix (~1h). they asked for a runbook they can paste to their SRE: please include simple note to reach out if they still see >1s p95.

lin (eng-ml): FYI the underlying cause: for long seqs SDPA kernels produce larger L2 cache pressure and different kernel launch patterns. the heuristic change flipped which kernel was selected; we should update kernel selector to consider effective seq_len and token mixing. suggested fix: revert preference and then add selective prefer_sdpa when (seq_len < 1024) or matmul shape matches.

maria (eng-runtime): created GH issue: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/issues/4521 - title: "regression: sdpa/flashattention kernel preference causes p95 regressions for long-seq workloads". assigned to lin + ryan. linked to incident doc.

ryan (build): canary hotfix is up (2026-03-14T05:40Z) with SDPA disabled; preliminary metrics look promising. p95 for the sampled workload dropped to ~130ms. i'll promote after 15min stable.

ajay (eng-sre): promoted to hosted-prod at 05:58Z. monitoring: p95 back to 140ms, p99 ~260ms for sampled traffic. rolling-forward routing change to remove per-customer fallback in 1h after stability.

maria (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add a regression test in CI that runs long-seq latency profile on new kernel selection changes, 2) update runtime kernel selector heuristics to be shape-aware, 3) postmortem and customer communication.

sam (customer-success): customer updated: thanks for fast response, will escalate internally if anything persists.

ajay (eng-sre): closing immediate on-call action items. leaving tasks in the incident board for follow-up.

maria (eng-runtime): recording notes for postmortem: root cause = heuristic flip in 6f3a2b8; mitigations = runtime env override + routing + hotfix build; permanent fix = selector heuristics + CI latency tests.

ryan (build): next steps: patch in build system to allow compile-time flag matrix testing in CI so this doesn't slip again.

lin (eng-ml): i'll draft a targeted kernel selector patch and a short benchmark script for gating.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. tagging incident for postmortem and customer follow-up. :white_check_mark:
